title: Signals of account takeover — question explanation
learningObjective: Identify account-takeover signals and initiate trusted account-recovery steps
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: You receive an email alert for a successful login from an unfamiliar location. Your account recovery email and forwarding rules also appear to have changed.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Identify account-takeover signals and initiate trusted account-recovery steps
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option C: Use a known official account-recovery route from a trusted device, contact support/security and report the unauthorized changes. Treat the signals as possible account compromise and use trusted recovery and containment procedures.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: The alert itself may be spoofed; its link should not be trusted without verification. Option B: A single change does not address potentially stolen credentials, active sessions or other persistence. Option D: Waiting may allow the intruder to maintain access or intercept future messages.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Contact the service or organizational identity team using a known route. Follow instructions to secure credentials, sessions, recovery methods and mailbox rules. Unexpected logins plus changed recovery settings are strong account-compromise indicators.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Unexpected logins plus changed recovery settings are strong account-compromise indicators.
